samples.text: Secondly, Africa looks forward to addressing economic development and joining the revolutions currently taking place in the fields of artificial intelligence, digitalization and renewable energy.

When presenting its voluntary national review report in July 2026, Algeria outlined the progress it has achieved in implementing the 17 SDGs and the efforts that it has made in that regard. Efforts that gained their true substance when those numbers became tangible improvements in all aspects of life. And this is the essence of development, transforming public policies into tangible dignity that people feel in their daily lives. And from this understanding of sustainable development, Algeria proceeds with the conviction that development cannot be fully complete unless it includes its regional surroundings and environment and unless it contributes to building a more integrated African space that is better able to face the present and future challenges. The destiny of the peoples of the continent is interconnected. Their challenges are shared. This makes solidarity and integration in Africa, indispensable pillars of sustainable development. As we witness the accelerating technological revolution, we cannot accept that Africa would remain on the margins or simply become a consumer of its outputs. Here we note the need to invest in the African person to build scientific and digital capacities so that artificial intelligence becomes a tool for development, not a new label for another development gap between the North and the South. We call for a balanced and responsible international regulation of artificial intelligence that would guarantee equitable access to its benefits, that would preserve the sovereignty of states, and that would transform this revolution into a shared opportunity rather than an exclusive privilege or monopoly in the hands of a few. In the end, we return to the question where we began. How do we restore trust? Trust is restored when words match actions. Trust is restored when the law is applied equally to all. Trust is restored when peoples can see the United Nations as a common home, a shared home, rather than an organization held hostage to the dominance of power politics. Our responsibility today is not to leave to our children a legacy of a world that is burdened with our crises.
